notYet: Not yet part of North Africa and Italy

stages.name: Italy, Rome's homeland
stages.desc: The ruling city and its Italian heartland

stages.name: Client kingdom
stages.desc: Numidian or Mauretanian kings, allied to Rome

stages.name: Free Punic city
stages.desc: Self-governing under sufetes, Punic in speech and stone

stages.name: Punic-speaking under Rome
stages.desc: Roman rule, but Punic still spoken and carved in inscriptions

stages.name: Roman province
stages.desc: Ruled by a Roman governor; taxes go to Rome

stages.name: Roman colonia
stages.desc: Colonies and towns of Roman citizens set the tone

states.name: Morocco
timeline: The kingdom of Mauretania, with old Punic towns such as Lixus on its coast
King Bocchus I hands Jugurtha to Rome and is rewarded with western Numidia
Juba II and Cleopatra Selene rule Mauretania from Caesarea
Caligula has King Ptolemy killed; Mauretania rises in revolt
Claudius makes Mauretania Tingitana a Roman province
Volubilis, still led by sufetes, is made a municipium for its loyalty

states.name: Libya
timeline: Numidian kings hold the Emporia, the Punic coastal towns of Tripolitania
Leptis Magna allies with Rome in the Jugurthine War: a free Punic city ruled by sufetes
Caesar fines Leptis for backing Juba; it stays a free city inside the Roman province
The sufete Annobal Tapapius Rufus gives Leptis a new market
Annobal Tapapius Rufus dedicates the theatre in Latin and Punic
Leptis and Oea go to war over their borders; Oea calls in the Garamantes
Under Vespasian, Leptis becomes a municipium, keeping its sufetes and its Punic
Trajan makes Leptis a colonia; the sufetes give way to duoviri
Lucius Septimius Severus is born at Leptis, into its Punic-descended elite
Severus grants his home town Italian rights and rebuilds it in marble

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage is razed; its lands become the province of Africa, governed from Utica
Gaius Gracchus founds the colony of Junonia on Carthage's site; it is soon annulled
After Thapsus, Caesar enlarges Roman Africa; Cato dies at Utica
Augustus settles Roman colonists at Carthage, the new capital of Africa; inland towns still write Punic

states.name: Italy
timeline: Rome, mistress of Italy, destroys Carthage and turns to Africa
Jugurtha is paraded in Marius's triumph and dies in a Roman prison
Septimius Severus of Leptis Magna enters Rome as emperor
The Senate dedicates the Arch of Septimius Severus in the Forum

states.name: Algeria
timeline: The Numidian kingdom of Micipsa, son of Masinissa, ruled from Cirta
Jugurtha seizes Cirta and kills the Italian traders there; Rome goes to war
Jugurtha is betrayed; Numidia survives under kings chosen by Rome
Juba I falls; his kingdom becomes Africa Nova, but Cirta and its towns go on writing Punic
Augustus makes the young Juba II king of Numidia
Juba II moves to Mauretania; Numidia is absorbed into Africa, still Punic-speaking
Tacfarinas leads the Musulamii in a seven-year revolt against Rome
Trajan founds Timgad for veterans; Roman colonies spread across Numidia
Hadrian reviews the Third Augustan Legion at Lambaesis

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: Scipio Aemilianus burns Carthage after a three-year siege; the survivors are sold into slavery.

events.title: Utica the capital
events.text: Utica, which sided with Rome, becomes the seat of the governor of the new province of Africa.

events.title: The Royal Ditch
events.text: A ditch, the Fossa Regia, marks the border between Roman Africa and the Numidian kingdom.

events.title: Colonia Junonia
events.text: Gaius Gracchus founds a Roman colony on Carthage's ruins; the Senate soon annuls it.

events.title: Micipsa dies
events.text: The Numidian king dies at Cirta, leaving his kingdom to two sons and his nephew Jugurtha.

events.title: Siege of Cirta
events.text: Jugurtha takes Cirta, kills his cousin Adherbal and massacres Italian traders; Rome declares war.

events.title: Leptis turns to Rome
events.text: Leptis Magna asks Rome for friendship and alliance and receives a small garrison.

events.title: Jugurtha betrayed
events.text: King Bocchus of Mauretania hands Jugurtha over to the young quaestor Sulla.

events.title: Jugurtha in Rome
events.text: Jugurtha walks in chains in Marius's triumph and dies in the prison beneath the Capitol.

events.title: Pompey in Africa
events.text: The young Pompey defeats Rome's exiled Marians and their Numidian ally near Utica.

events.title: Battle of Thapsus
events.text: Julius Caesar crushes the Pompeians and their ally, King Juba I of Numidia.

events.title: Cato at Utica
events.text: Rather than accept Caesar's pardon, Cato the Younger takes his own life at Utica.

events.title: Juba's fall
events.text: Juba I dies in a suicide pact near Zama; his kingdom becomes the province of Africa Nova.

events.title: Leptis fined
events.text: Caesar fines Leptis three million pounds of olive oil a year for siding with Juba.

events.title: Caesar's colony
events.text: Weeks before his murder, Caesar decrees a Roman colony on the site of Carthage.

events.title: Carthage reborn
events.text: Augustus settles thousands of colonists at Colonia Iulia Concordia Carthago, the new capital of Africa.

events.title: Juba II's Mauretania
events.text: Juba II and his wife Cleopatra Selene rule Mauretania from Iol, renamed Caesarea.

events.title: Market of Leptis
events.text: The sufete Annobal Tapapius Rufus pays for a new market for his city.

events.title: Theatre of Leptis
events.text: Annobal Tapapius Rufus dedicates the theatre with inscriptions in Latin and Punic.

events.title: Tacfarinas rises
events.text: A Numidian former auxiliary, Tacfarinas, leads the Musulamii in a long war against Rome.

events.title: Juba II dies
events.text: The scholar-king dies at Caesarea; his son Ptolemy inherits Mauretania.

events.title: Tacfarinas killed
events.text: The rebel leader dies fighting at Auzia, ending a seven-year revolt.

events.title: Last king of Mauretania
events.text: Caligula summons King Ptolemy and has him executed; his freedman Aedemon leads a revolt.

events.title: Two Mauretanias
events.text: Claudius divides the kingdom into the provinces of Tingitana and Caesariensis.

events.title: Volubilis rewarded
events.text: Claudius makes Volubilis, whose leaders bore the Punic title of sufete, a municipium.

events.title: Leptis against Oea
events.text: A border feud between Leptis and Oea draws in Garamantian raiders until a Roman legate drives them off.

events.title: Leptis a municipium
events.text: Under Vespasian Leptis gains Roman municipal status but keeps its sufetes.

events.title: Timgad founded
events.text: Trajan founds the colony of Thamugadi for veterans of the Third Augustan Legion.

events.title: Leptis a colonia
events.text: Trajan makes Leptis a Roman colony and its free people Roman citizens.

events.title: Hadrian at Lambaesis
events.text: Emperor Hadrian watches the Third Augustan Legion drill and praises it in a speech carved in stone.

events.title: Severus born
events.text: Lucius Septimius Severus is born at Leptis on 11 April, to a family of Punic descent.

events.title: Apuleius on trial
events.text: At Sabratha, the writer Apuleius mocks a young rival of the elite for speaking only Punic.

events.title: Legate in Africa
events.text: Severus serves in Africa as legate of the proconsul at Carthage.

events.title: Caracalla born
events.text: At Lugdunum, where Severus is governor, Julia Domna gives birth to their son Caracalla.

events.title: Emperor Severus
events.text: After the murder of Pertinax, Severus marches on Rome and is recognised as emperor.

events.title: Battle of Lugdunum
events.text: Severus defeats his last rival, Clodius Albinus, in a vast battle outside Lugdunum.

events.title: Desert forts
events.text: A fort is built at Gholaia (Bu Njem) to guard Tripolitania from the desert peoples.

events.title: Arch in the Forum
events.text: The Senate dedicates a triumphal arch to Severus and his sons in the Roman Forum.

events.title: Return to Leptis
events.text: Severus visits his home city, grants it Italian rights and rebuilds it in marble.

events.title: Ashes to Rome
events.text: Severus dies at York on 4 February; his ashes are laid in Hadrian's mausoleum in Rome.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Italy, by the status of each country's ancient heartland: Tunisia stands for Carthage's old lands, Algeria for Numidia, Morocco for Mauretania and Libya for Tripolitania and Leptis Magna. Regions are today's boundaries and the vast Saharan areas swing the shares. It is a simplification: kingdoms, free cities, colonies and Punic-speaking towns existed side by side.
